questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Use the good tire's brake and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the good tire's brake and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat, grip both handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep going straight. If you must brake, slowly use the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do when turning?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help your balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect you?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most drugs for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or nerves cause drowsiness and may make riding unsafe. Always know how a medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to share it with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous by encouraging them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What should you do when you cannot avoid riding over an obstacle or uneven surface?

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Lift slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lift slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, approach it at close to a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible and keep the motorcycle upright. Lift slightly off your seat so your knees absorb some impact. Just before hitting it, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front end.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They are caused by bald tires.
They happen at speeds above 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders who have owned their motorcycle for less than six months. Most crashes happen during the day when riders are traveling at low speeds.

questions.question: Why should you use both front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake causes uneven wear.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
It is the only way to slow a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes in normal stops creates a habit of always using both. This habit is helpful in emergencies, where using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals are important for group riding. When a lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, the group should stop.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your fingers on the clutch and both brake levers. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can the body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: On average, the body eliminates about one drink per hour. The time needed to lower blood alcohol content varies, so do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: At night, how should your following distance compare to the daytime?

options.text: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
You should allow a shorter following distance at night.
You should always maintain the same following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distance in the dark because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts clearly. Always use a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: For routine braking, what should you do?

options.text: Alternate between the front and rear brakes.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When someone tailgates you, what should you do?

options.text: Focus on the road ahead and ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster, which is more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: You lose the ability to change direction.
It is only a problem if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is very dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure can lock the rear wheel. When this happens, you cannot change direction. You must release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator stop other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center portion of the lane
By riding in the left portion of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves no large spaces on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Keep them busy with other activities.
Keep them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: There are several ways to stop someone from riding while impaired. You can arrange another ride, involve them in other activities, prevent them from leaving before they are sober, and ask other friends to help prevent them from riding.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before starting to pass. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between the cars to pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between slow or parked cars puts you at risk of hitting open car doors or being hit by cars pulling into traffic. You will not have room to escape if a hazard appears. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when stopping quickly.
Should only be used on slippery surfaces.
Is not as strong as the rear brake.
Is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: When braking on a surface with poor grip, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes faster than normal.
Apply the brakes slower and gentler than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes slower and gentler than normal.
questions.explanation: When stopping on a slippery surface, use caution. Apply the brakes gently and slowly.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ as likely to die in a crash as riders with helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are usually white with black letters or symbols. They show traffic rules like speed limits. Follow the rules on these signs.
